complexity.correctness_reason: Recursion depth equals the word length and the limit is hard-coded to 2000, so once the 1000-character cap is lifted, inserting or searching a word longer than ~2000 characters raises RecursionError.
complexity.notes: The word[1:] slicing copies the remaining string at every recursion level, so each operation costs O(L^2) time instead of the usual O(L) for an iterative trie walk, and the recursion stack holds O(L^2) bytes of slices transiently. Keys are single characters from a bounded alphabet, so dict lookups are O(1) worst case. sys.setrecursionlimit is mutated as a side effect of every node construction, which is poor style (it also runs per-node, needlessly).
complexity.summary: A recursive trie where each node is itself a PrefixTree with a dict of children keyed by first character; each call strips the first character via word[1:] and recurses, marking terminal nodes with a present flag.
